correctness.rationale: For each nonreal conjugate pair, spectral mapping Z=(θI+S)^{-1}(θS−I) yields modal polynomial (λ−a)^2=−ω²τ²λ. The invariant c=|(τ−i)/(τ+i)|=|(μ−i)/(μ+i)|, together with 0<Im τ≤2√r/(1+r) when r=ρ(L)<1, implies q=(1−c)/(1+c)≤2√r/(1+r), so r≥(1−sqrt(1−q²))/(1+sqrt(1−q²)). Equality forces τ=iq and ω=1+R*, with uniquely prescribed nonzero θ for u≠0. For u=0,v≠1, τ=iq only at θ boundary 0 or infinity and minimum is a nonattained infimum. Direct example u=1,v=2 has θ=√5−2 and rate ≈0.03940575785, while unpreconditioned SOR has no convergent real relaxation for v≥1. This is a spectral, not transient-norm, theorem and needs no diagonalizability.
